what: The Catch and the Bowl's ground-layer set, for the preview host krator/catch_bowl.gd and its shader shaders/catch_bowl_ground.gdshader. Six desert layers in the six roles godot/shaders/terrain.gdshader gives the layer indices, so when the region is cut the set drops into the 1:1 shader's selectors without being repacked. The preview binds it to its own samplers rather than the global uniforms, because it is not on the chunk pipeline that sets those.

style.where: openworld/catch-bowl/PLAN.md; the region is not cut yet, so nothing reads this but the preview host

layers.name: sand_dune
layers.ground: the ergs: the Bowl's sand seas and the Catch's drifts, the only ground the dune lines are drawn on
layers.note: the shader's erg mask picks it; tile at 2.4 m so a dune's flank reads as sand and not as gravel

layers.name: salt_crust
layers.ground: the Bowl's salt pan below sea level and the Catch's sabkhas: the brightest ground in the region
layers.note: the wet role, because a sabkha is where the water was

layers.name: ironstone
layers.ground: the benches and the high desert pavement above the sand line, dark with desert varnish
layers.note: the high role: what the uplands are, not alpine turf

layers.name: reg_gravel
layers.ground: the reg: gravel plains swept clean of sand, between the ergs
layers.note: the province mask's other half; ground.gravel019 is coarser and is the scree's layer

layers.name: slickrock
layers.ground: the scarps, the Godsgate's walls and every slope too steep for sand to lie on
layers.note: tiled large: a scarp seen from a kilometre wants metres a tile, not centimetres

layers.name: scree
layers.ground: the talus below the scarps, where the shader's scree layer already puts its relief
layers.note: the pave role has no paving here; the Catch has no made roads
